BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

 IN THE MATTER OF SOUTHWESTERN PUBLIC                                    )
 SERVICE COMPANY’S APPLICATION FOR: (1)                                  )
 REVISION OF ITS RETAIL RATES UNDER ADVICE                               ) Docket No. 25-00079-UT
 NOTICE 341; AND (2) OTHER ASSOCIATED RELIEF                             )
                                                                         )

                                 PRE-HEARING BENCH REQUEST

        THIS MATTER comes before the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission

(“Commission”) upon Southwestern Public Service Company’s (“SPS”) Application for Authority

to Change Rates and for Other Approvals and Authorizations with Schedules A-1 through Q-6 (the

“Application”).

        The Commission issues this Order to collect information and testimony to assist in its

review of the Application.

                                           BACKGROUND

        1.       On November 20, 2025 1, SPS filed the Application requesting authority to change

its base rates and certain other approvals. 2 Specifically, SPS requests to increase its base rate

charges for the New Mexico retail jurisdiction by $175,354,544, a 24.25% increase over current

base rate revenue and 16.73% in total revenues, based on a total New Mexico retail revenue

requirements of $892,652,373 for the Future Test Year running from December 1, 2026, through

November 30, 2027. 3 The Application includes a request for an overall weighted average cost of

capital (“WACC”) of 8.21% for the Future Test Year, reflecting a 56% equity ratio, an authorized

return on equity (“ROE”) of 10.5%, and a cost of debt of 5.29%. 4



1 This order summarizes relevant background. The full electronic record of this proceeding is available at

https://e360.prc.nm.gov/portal/public/.
2 Application at 1.
3 Id. at 3.
4 Id.
         2.       On November 26, 2025, the Commission issued an order appointing Hearing

Examiner Patrick Schaefer to preside over this matter. 5

        3.       On December 11, 2025, the Commission suspended the Application’s

accompanying Advice Notice 341 for an initial period of nine months to hold a hearing concerning

the reasonableness of the proposed rate. 6

                                             DISCUSSION

        4.       Upon review of the Application, this Pre-Hearing Bench Request requests that SPS

provide or otherwise identify information relevant to the Commission in determining whether the

Application is fair, just, and reasonable.

        5.       The Public Utility Act (“PUA”) establishes a policy of requiring that reasonable

and proper services are available at fair, just, and reasonable rates while permitting the

encouragement of capital and investment. 7 The PUA grants the Commission authority to advance

this policy. It grants the Commission general and exclusive power and jurisdiction to regulate and

supervise every public utility in respect to its rates and service regulations 8 and to ensure that rates

are just and reasonable. 9 To determine whether a rate is just and reasonable, the Commission must

balance investors’ interests against ratepayers’ interests. 10 The Commission is granted great

flexibility in the method used to determine whether rates align with the goals of the PUA. 11

        6.       To assist the Commission in determining whether the proposed Application is fair,

just, and reasonable, the Commission seeks the following information:

6 See generally Order Suspending Advice Notice 341 (Dec. 11, 2025).

10 State v. Mountain States Tel. & Tel. Co. 1950-NMSC-055, ⁋ 39, 54 N.M. 315.
11 Southern Union Gas Co. v. New Mexico Public Service Commission, 1972-NMSC-072, ⁋ 2, 84 N.M. 330.

                a. The number of kilowatt hours (kWh) consumed per month and (if applicable)
                  demand (kW) metered per month, by an average-use customer within each of
                  SPS’s customer classes.
               b. For (a) each class of service, (b) separately for the summer and non-summer
                  months, and (c) for various levels of use:
                        i. The monthly bill under current rates stating separately the customer
                           charge, usage charge, any demand charge, the Fuel and Purchased
                           Power Cost Adjustment Clause (FPPCAC) charge, any other separate
                           charges (such as the renewable energy and energy efficiency rider
                           charges) but excluding taxes and surcharges and the total bill.
                       ii. The monthly bill under proposed rates separately stating the customer
                           charge, usage charge, any demand charge, the FPPCAC charge, any
                           other separate charges (such as the renewable energy and energy
                           efficiency rider charges) but excluding taxes and surcharges and the
                           total bill.
               c. The amounts of executive compensation, by position, that SPS seeks to recover
                  in its cost of service.
               d. SPS’s approved non-fuel revenue requirement in Case No. 22-00287-UT.
               e. SPS’s requested non-fuel revenue requirement in this case.
               f. What is the base cost of fuel (per kWh) incorporated into SPS’s existing rates?
               g. What is the base cost of fuel incorporated into SPS’s proposed rates? Provide
                  the anticipated dollar cost of fuel for the test year and the anticipated billing
                  units expressed in kWh used to determine the base cost of fuel.
               h. If SPS were to collect all of its fuel costs through base rates, what would be the
                  base cost of fuel incorporated into new rates taking effect on January 1, 2027
                  (or whenever the proposed rates become effective)?
               i. A loads and resources table showing both current loads and resources and the
                  projected loads and resources once projects currently approved and under
                  construction are brought into service.
               j. SPS’s support for its position on the proposed recovery of its rate case and
                  litigation expenses including discussion of the following:
                        i. If SPS is seeking recovery of all or a portion of its rate case and litigation
                           expenses, why should expenses be approved for recovery?
                       ii. If SPS is seeking recovery of the expenses incurred with appeals of rate
                           case decisions, why should these expenses be approved for recovery?
                      iii. If SPS is seeking any portion of the rate case expense be included in rate
                           base, is SPS also seeking a return on the expenses? If so, why should a
                           return be authorized on the expense, and what return should be
                           authorized?
                      iv. Should rate case expenses and litigation expenses be treated similarly or
                           differently for ratemaking purposes? Provide support for your position.
               k. Break down the proposed revenue requirement by function, classification, cost
                  allocation, class allocation, and rate design in accordance with the table attached
                  to this Bench Request as Exhibit A.
               l. A list of issues and costs previously raised, which the Commission deferred to
                  this rate case and the dockets in which those issues were previously raised.

                m. A list of Rule 440 Reports, filed since SPS's last rate case, that are included in
                  the Application, along with the associated costs. For each cost, indicate whether
                  it relates to generation, transmission, distribution facilities, or a combination of
                  these categories.
               n. A list of SPS regulatory assets or other items currently being recovered through
                  rate riders. An explanation of whether those existing rate riders should be
                  modified, terminated, or rolled into the rate base.
               o. What are the specific percentage changes in cost allocation for New Mexico
                  retail, Texas retail, and wholesale jurisdictions from the Base Period to the
                  Future Test Year, and what is the detailed breakdown of the projected load
                  driving these changes in the New Mexico retail jurisdiction?
               p. Are any of the costs SPS proposes to allocate solely to the New Mexico
                  jurisdiction the result of SPS’s efforts to comply with New Mexico’s Energy
                  Transition Act? 12 If so, what are the costs for ETA compliance for New Mexico
                  retail customers?
                               FINDINGS AND CONCLUSIONS

       7.      The Commission finds that requiring SPS to provide documentation or testimony

on these issues or otherwise identify where this information can be found within the Application

will assist the Commission’s evaluation of the Application.

        IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

       A.      On or before March 13, 2026, SPS shall file supplemental testimony responding to

the questions set out in Paragraph 6 of this Order. If SPS has already submitted documentation or

testimony on these matters, the company may direct the Commission to the location in the record

where responsive materials can be found.

       B.      Staff and intervenors may include a response to SPS’s answer to this Bench Request

in their direct testimony, which is due on March 27, 2026. Alternatively, Staff and intervenors may

request additional time to respond to the specific information SPS provided as a result of this

Bench Request.

       C.      This Order is effective when signed.
